questions.questionText: What is a reason why firms making similar products sometimes locate near each other?

options.text: competition is decreased
there are external economies of scale
there are internal economies of scale
transport costs may be eliminated

questions.questionText:
To achieve horizontal integration a record company producing compact discs (CDs) could merge
with another firm.
What would this firm most likely be doing?

options.text: owning shops selling CDs
producing CDs
producing CD players
producing machinery used in the making of CDs

questions.questionText: What is a difference between a monopoly and a perfectly competitive firm?

options.text: A monopoly always has economies of scale and a perfectly competitive firm has diseconomies of scale.
A monopoly always operates in the public sector and a perfectly competitive firm always operates in the private sector.
A monopoly is a price maker and a perfectly competitive firm is a price taker.
A monopoly seeks to maximise profits and a perfectly competitive firm seeks to maximise output.

questions.questionText: Which aim of government policy is most likely to be achieved by an increase in interest rates?

options.text: economic growth
greater equality of income
full employment
price stability

questions.questionText: Why might a government encourage a monopoly?

options.text: It can have high average costs.
It can compete against foreign firms.
It can prevent innovation.
It can make excessive profits.

questions.questionText:
Which combination of government policies is most likely to be successful at reducing
unemployment?

options.text: budgeting for a surplus and lowering interest rates
budgeting for a deficit and raising interest rates
budgeting for a surplus and raising interest rates
budgeting for a deficit and lowering interest rates

questions.questionText:
A government wishes to raise the general standard of living in its country.
In the short run, which policy would be the most likely to achieve this aim?

options.text: preventing the merger of two companies into a monopoly
raising taxation to repay government debts
reducing the rate of income tax while maintaining the services it provides
spending more on roads in rural areas rather than in city centres

questions.questionText:
Sam wrote a list of how he would prefer to spend his Saturday afternoon.
first choice go to a cricket match
second choice watch the annual town parade
third choice go to the cinema
fourth choice visit relatives
Unfortunately a thunderstorm caused the cricket match and the town parade to be cancelled.
Sam went to the cinema.
What was the opportunity cost of going to the cinema?

options.text: going to the cricket match
watching the town parade
visiting his relatives
losing his Saturday free time

questions.questionText: How does a production possibility curve show that scarcity exists?

options.text: It shows that a rise in demand for one of the products increases its price.
It shows that as more resources are used to produce a product, its price rises.
It shows that at any point outside the production possibility curve an economy is wasting resources.
It shows that there is a limit to the quantity of products that can be produced with existing resources and technology.

questions.questionText:
In which case is it possible to set the level of reward before production takes place for the first
factor of production but not for the second?
first factor second factor

options.text: capital land
enterprise labour
labour capital
land enterprise

questions.questionText:
In the 2016 Olympics in Brazil, the opening ceremony will take place in the Maracana Stadium,
which can seat 82 000 spectators. It is expected that all tickets for the ceremony will be sold
quickly, leaving many people dissatisfied.
What can be concluded from this?

options.text: Price elasticity of demand for tickets will be perfectly elastic.
Some people will be able to resell their tickets at a higher price than they paid for them.
The Olympic authority will make more tickets available for sale.
This will be an example of market failure.

questions.questionText:
In 2011, a company selling milk in glass bottles replaced them with new plastic bottles. When
they were introduced, the equilibrium quantity on the market fell.
What could be a reason for this fall?

options.text: Consumers preferred the new bottle because it was lighter to carry.
Milk from the farms used to fill the bottle cost more.
The bottle was cheaper than the existing glass bottle to produce.
The new bottle was introduced with a successful advertising campaign.

questions.questionText: Which change would make the supply of a product more price elastic?

options.text: an increase in the number of close substitutes for the product
an increase in the proportion of firms working at full capacity
a reduction in the time taken to make the product
a reduction in the time that the product can be stored

questions.questionText:
Developers want to increase the size of a major retail shopping area in a city. It is thought that the
proposal would create hundreds of jobs, be profitable for the shops but cause major traffic
congestion.
What economic concepts are involved in this statement?

options.text: external cost and private benefit
income distribution and inelastic demand
private investment and a decrease in supply
social benefit and perfect competition

questions.questionText: Which will encourage domestic producers to grow more maize?

options.text: granting subsidies to maize producers
increasing the sales tax on maize
removing guaranteed minimum prices for maize
removing quotas on imported maize

questions.questionText:
What will be the most likely effect of a fall in interest rates on saving and borrowing?
saving borrowing

options.text: decrease decrease
decrease increase
increase decrease
increase increase

questions.questionText: When will a trade union find it easier to achieve higher wages for its members?

options.text: when consumers demand more of the product made
when the company has a decrease in profits
when the cost of raw materials increases
when unemployment increases

questions.questionText: What might be a direct benefit to the individual worker of a specialised job?

options.text: Specialisation enables a better quality product to be produced.
Specialisation enables the firm to introduce more machinery.
Specialisation enables the worker to become more skilled.
Specialisation makes better use of resources.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the change in real incomes for a number of occupations between 1978 and
2008.
change in real income
occupation
doctors 153
lawyers 114
accountants 60
bricklayers 37
bus and coach drivers 19
fork-lift truck drivers –5
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: All occupations were better off in 2008 than in 1978.
Fork-lift truck drivers earned the lowest wages in 2008.
Doctors have earned more than lawyers since 1978.
Professionals received higher percentage increases in income than manual workers.

questions.questionText: Which function of money enables people to compare the worth of different products?

options.text: medium of exchange
standard for deferred payments
store of value
unit of account

questions.questionText: Which of the following could not be a reason for imposing tariffs on imported goods?

options.text: to encourage self sufficiency
to lower the general price level within the economy
to protect a growing domestic industry
to reduce a balance of trade deficit

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an export of Jamaica?

options.text: a loan to Jamaica by the International Monetary Fund
Jamaican holidays taken by American tourists
dividends paid by a company in Jamaica to its American shareholders
sales of Japanese cars in Jamaica

questions.questionText:
A developing country’s two major sources of income from international trade are fishing and
tourism.
If the country’s exchange rate depreciated, what is likely to happen?

options.text: Imported goods would become cheaper for local people.
The country would definitely become poorer.
The price of fish sold as exports would become cheaper.
Tourists to the country would be discouraged by higher prices.

questions.questionText:
In some developing countries a large percentage of the population is involved in subsistence
farming.
What can be concluded from this?

options.text: Each family will be able to produce enough to live on.
Production is unlikely to be capital intensive.
Production will be efficient.
There will be a high level of trade.

questions.questionText:
A country has a falling birth rate and a rising death rate while an increasing number of its working
age adults (16-60 years) are seeking employment abroad.
How will this probably affect the numbers in the different age groups in the country?
under 16 years 16-60 years over 60 years

options.text: fall fall fall
fall rise rise
rise fall rise
rise rise fall

questions.questionText: Which would best indicate the start of an economic recession?

options.text: falling interest rates
fluctuating levels of employment
negative growth of GDP
steadily increasing price levels

questions.questionText:
The table shows the change in the labour force in Bangladesh between 2006 and 2009.
group 2006 (millions) 2009 (millions)
urban male labour force 8.9 9.7
urban female labour force 2.8 3.1
total urban labour force 11.7 12.8
rural male labour force 28.5 30.5
rural female labour force 9.3 10.4
total rural labour force 37.8 40.9
Which statement is most likely to be consistent with these statistics?

options.text: Farming is the major employer in the economy.
Male workers are more mobile than female workers.
The absolute increase in the labour force is greater in urban areas than rural areas.

The supply of female workers has fallen.
